name: fx
tagline: A native coding-agent CLI written in Zig with an embeddable runtime.
hook: Requires a real interaction with the freshly built binary before declaring work ready, because tests can miss TTY and thread-lifetime failures.
summary: fx requires runtime evidence from the binary just built, not only a green test run. The guide also covers architecture, Zig style, exact-commit CI, repeatable terminal replays, performance limits, and the difference between optimizer training and correctness checks.

techniques.title: Explain what passing tests do not establish
techniques.body: The opening gate names runtime setup that tests may omit: the full application, a TTY, and background threads. It requires a real interaction before a completion claim, with an explicit limitation when the environment cannot run the binary.
techniques.quote: A passing test suite is necessary, not sufficient — tests in this repo do not always construct the full runtime, attach a TTY, or spawn background threads, so they will not catch startup crashes, render regressions, or thread-lifetime bugs.

techniques.title: Bind verification to the binary containing the change
techniques.body: The guide requires the newly built executable from the checkout and explains why an installed version on PATH is not evidence. It also tells agents to investigate an incomplete fix rather than immediately blame the user's binary.
techniques.quote: * `zig build` writes to `zig-out/bin/fx`. That is the only binary that contains your latest change.

techniques.title: Separate optimizer training from correctness coverage
techniques.body: Every root E2E file must be classified as training, verification-only, or intentionally excluded from the optimization corpus. Rare or security-sensitive behavior can remain mandatory to pass without influencing hot-path optimization.
techniques.quote:
* **Verification-only:** important correctness, recovery, security, or rare
  behavior that the final candidate must pass without making it hot

techniques.title: Turn a live terminal failure into replayable evidence
techniques.body: The render-debugging section records output bytes and resize events in a deterministic tape. It then routes the reproduced failure into an in-process regression test, connecting manual observation with a repeatable check.
techniques.quote: The tape is deterministic — any reviewer can replay it without a TTY, and a golden file can be checked in as a regression test.

techniques.title: Name the authoritative environment for a performance budget
techniques.body: Linux CI owns the raw startup-latency contract. Local macOS results remain informational because loader and process overhead vary; the guide forbids subtracting a baseline to manufacture a passing result.
techniques.quote:
The
process baseline is diagnostic only and is never subtracted.

techniques.title: Tie CI evidence to the current revision
techniques.body: The readiness rule rejects stale or partial CI results and requires all four native platform aggregates to pass. A follow-up repair needs a new run on its own commit.
techniques.quote: A Full CI result is valid only when it belongs to the exact current commit and all four `Full suite (...)` jobs succeed.
